reason: B is the better test because its 50% Hf substitution makes the targeted ≥10% density reduction more quantitatively plausible and it specifies strain rate, phase characterization, and a composition-specific rejection criterion. Its single-phase-BCC mechanism remains questionable because Al can promote ordering or secondary phases, but A’s claimed 15–20% density reduction from only 30% Hf replacement is implausible and its “if any alloy fails” falsification rule is logically overbroad.
